title: Why Aren't There Any Films About Ancient Babylon?

commenti.body:
I think it's in line with what you're saying but simpler: what is the hook for Babylon? Basically all movies made about Rome, Greece or Egypt are similar and fall into three or so categories. One is sword and sandal involving chariots and gladiators, etc. (recently that would be Gladiator, the Spartacus show); the second is some kind of fantasy involving in the gods (Hercules, The Mummy, Clash of the Titans, etc.); then there are specific historical events or people (Pompeii, Cleopatra, Caesar). I don't think there is any awareness at all about any of that stuff for Babylon. People mostly have no idea of key events or people so there just isn't an obvious movie to make. Not that it couldn't happen but it would have to be sold entirely on its own.

There's probably a good reason for all this too. For Rome/Greece we have the Bible and Christian culture. That led to the interest in sword and sandal, biblical epics, etc. and a broader knowledge of the time period because of the Bible and Christ. For Egypt you have the cultural boom in the late 1800s/early 1900s due to the excavation of the historical sites and periods; that has continued through to today. Babylon has never had that kind of way in to modern historical interest.

As you say, for a historical movie, you will need a story with characters you care for in a setting that you know something about.  Which characters do you, or the general public,  know from Ancient Babylonia or broader Mesopotamia?  I sure would know none without looking it up and I am not even sure there are any.

So little is known from Babylonians that it would be more a fantasy movie than anything based on history.  Then why bother to set it there?

The reason for it is the same as why Spielberg’s Montezuma film hasn’t been made. Nobody wants to take the risk. 

To push back a little bit on what you said I think Babylon absolutely has a visual style, it’s just unfamiliar to most. Think of the Lamassu statues, the Ishtar gate, or the Code of Hammurabi. There exists a striking style but mainly relegated to museums and scholars. 

Why spend what is likely going be a huge amount of money on a film about a period with which most people are unfamiliar? Just make another Rome or Egypt film. To go back to the mesoamerican example there’s one big budget film about that period: Apocalypto. It made its money back but little has been done in that period and part of the world since. 

I too wish that stories from other cultures would be adapted, it’s almost a travesty the Epic of Gilgamesh hasn’t been done on film yet. Eventually someone with a modicum of power or weight to throw around will decide to make a movie about these lesser known cultures, but they will be stymied by the moneymen every step of the way.

I mean, Babylon would be a cool-looking setting with alien architecture we're not used to seeing on film. A film set there could just use Babylon as a backdrop to tell a very human story; it doesn't necessarily have to be based on any historical figures. A fictional story set there would be unique enough imo since we've never really seen the city depicted in all it's splendour before
